evidence: Runtime facts, each matched against what test.sh actually does: entry path /app/server.js and data at /app/app.db (instruction.md:5; integration.md:3); start command 'Node 22 running /app/server.js as an ordinary user and not necessarily from inside /app' (integration.md:3) matches test.sh 'setsid env -i ... setpriv --reuid=65534 ... node "$APP_ENTRY"', where the entry may be the /tmp/submission copy; port 3000 on 0.0.0.0 (integration.md:3) matches the probe and judge URLs; storage at /app/app.db or DB_PATH (integration.md:3) matches test.sh DB_PATH="$APP_DB"; all five injected env vars (PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME which may not be /app, PORT=3000, DB_PATH) are named (integration.md:3); health path GET /api/health returns 200 even if the DB cannot open (integration.md:3) matches probe_ready; fixed clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z, displayed in UTC (integration.md:7), agrees with seed 'clock'; seed /assets/seed_data.json, copied into /app and imported once (instruction.md:5; integration.md:5); restart persistence of every state kind (integration.md:5) covers the functional persistence/restart_app criterion; no symlinks in /app (integration.md:5) matches test.sh, which exits with reward 0 on non-node_modules links; accounts and password123 (walls-and-retention.md:3-11) agree with seed accounts and app_context.md. Network is public and external assets are explicitly allowed (integration.md:3), so no offline constraint is needed. Coverage, criterion by criterion: the render gate (pre-sign-in privacy instruction.md:7; wrong password implied by the shared password) and the constraints gate (post and cross-account readback, instruction.md:1,9). Functional, all 16: client scope, signed-out data (integration.md:9; walls-and-retention.md:17), every wall route, mentions, links and suggestions (walls:15-19; conversations.md:17,21), live wall (walls:19), nested replies with quotes and the cross-matter reply ban (conversations:5), deleted/expired placeholders, exact-age expiry and edit-not-younger (walls:23-25; conversations:9), timer changes and versions purge (walls:23-25), hold scope, partner-only and release (walls:29), stale edit, author-only edit/delete and mention follow-edits (conversations:9,21), safe formatting everywhere including snippets and transcripts (conversations:13), message links and the not-available preview (conversations:17), per-person cross-tab unread, the new-messages line, mark-unread and deleted-not-counted (conversations:25), duplicate send and same-time order (conversations:31), live updates that keep the draft and scroll (conversations:33), case-insensitive literal substring search without earlier versions (walls:33), transcript heading, threads, author, sent time, edited, hold and versions with no controls (walls:35), restart persistence (integration:5). Polish, all 6: Enter/Shift+Enter/Escape (conversations:29), delete confirm (conversations:9), highlight persisting (conversations:17), 390 px without sideways scroll (conversations:35), refusal reason staying in place (walls:37). Visual (matter list with unread counts, hold badge and timer notice, transcript, phone width) grades rendering of required surfaces only. Every literal a judge depends on exists in the seed: M-11/12/13 titles, K-10 vs K-11 at the exact seven-day boundary, the K-13 earlier version 2,400, the K-2 earlier version, the K-16 HTML, and Dev's wall. A plausible broken app that could pass, for example one that enforces walls only in the UI, ignores DB_PATH, or depends on cwd, is excluded because the brief states each fact and the criteria replay requests. I could not construct a conforming alternative that fails on an unstated fact. Minor observation, not a defect: 'sign out' (functional signin_and_client_scope Part A; polish refusal_in_place) is never named. It is implied by 'sign in as different people' (instruction.md:9) and by the account surface, which the skill's known false positives cover. No hidden technology mandate: SQLite is stated in integration.md:3, and no criterion prescribes routes. This row is static and needs no runtime measurement. It is not a claim that the configured judge run passes; no Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
